Hi, yeah, um... so I guess I'm here because things have just been feeling really off lately. Well, not *lately* lately, but ever since I started trying to, you know, clean up my image and my daily routine. I've been trying to get involved with this arts board stuff—it's a whole thing, and I really wanted to present myself well and take it seriously, so I thought I needed to completely overhaul how I do things to be more put-together. But instead of feeling better or more productive, I’ve just been... I don't know, so much more tense and down than I ever expected to be. 

Like, I thought getting organized would make me feel good, but it's having the opposite effect. I mean, I’m still doing the absolute basics of getting through the day, but I just keep dropping all these little things that I actually normally really care about. For example, I completely spaced on my fair planning notes the other day, and my design drafts are just sitting on my desk untouched, which is so unlike me because I usually love working on those and I'm usually so on top of it. And then, because I'm dropping the ball on the creative stuff I actually like, I just feel this immense guilt about it all the time. But then instead of, like, sitting down and just catching up on the drafts or the notes like a normal person, I just end up feeling terrible and canceling plans with people so I can stay home, even though I don't even use that time to catch up. It's just becoming this whole frustrating cycle and I don't really know how to snap out of it.

That's a really good question, actually. Because, you see, I think I *do* still like them? Like, in my head, I still love the idea of sitting down with my iPad and working on those design drafts. So it's less that I don't like the activities themselves anymore, and more that the whole environment around them in my brain has gotten so cluttered with this pressure I put on myself to be this perfect, put-together professional person. 

Which is so silly because I'm 23, I don't need to have it all figured out, but I just thought if I structured my day better, the enjoyment would actually go up, not get buried under all this guilt. So, yeah, I guess I still like the things I used to like, but the actual feeling of having fun while doing them is just totally missing right now because I can't get past the stress of it all. I just sit there and stare at the screen and think about how I'm failing at my new routine instead of just letting myself enjoy the art.

I mean, that's the thing, right? Like, what even counts as pleasure when everything feels so clouded? I've been trying to figure that out myself, honestly. Because it's not like I'm sitting in a dark room staring at the wall all day, but it also doesn't feel like I'm really... experiencing things the way I normally do. 

Like, the other day, my mom came over, and usually, we have this whole routine where we make tea—she always brings this specific chamomile blend she gets from a little shop near her house, which is so nice of her—and we sit and talk about whatever shows we're watching. And I did it, I went through the motions, I drank the tea, I talked about the latest episode of this baking show I’ve been trying to keep up with. But while I was doing it, I just felt... blank? Or not blank, exactly, but just sort of disconnected from it. Like, I knew I should be enjoying it, because I love my mom and I love that tea, but the actual feeling of happiness or comfort just wasn't there. 

And it's like that with everything right now. Even just taking a walk, which I used to do every morning to clear my head before I decided I needed to 'optimize' my schedule. Now, if I take a walk, I'm just thinking about how I'm wasting time, or how I should be doing something productive, or how I'm failing at being organized. So the walk isn't pleasurable anymore, it's just another thing I'm doing wrong. 

I don't know if that makes sense. It's just really frustrating because I want to enjoy things, I really do. I keep trying to force myself to do things that I know I usually like, hoping that the feeling will just magically come back. Like, 'okay, if I watch this funny movie, I'll laugh and feel better.' But then I watch it, and I might chuckle, but it doesn't reach that deeper level of actually feeling good. It's just all so surface-level right now, and underneath that surface, it's just this constant buzz of stress and guilt about not being the person I'm trying to be. So, to answer your question, I guess... no? Not really? At least, not in any way that actually feels meaningful or lasting.

Sleep? No, actually, my sleep has been totally fine, which is kind of surprising when you think about it. I mean, with all this buzzing in my head and the constant feeling of being behind on this perfect schedule I made for myself, you'd think I'd be tossing and turning all night, staring at the ceiling, right? I read this article once about how stress and guilt are the number one killers of a good night's sleep, especially for people in their twenties who are trying to figure their lives out. And it made so much sense to me at the time, because, you know, when you're lying in the dark, there's nothing to distract you from your own thoughts.

But for some reason, that hasn't happened to me. I still go to bed around eleven—well, sometimes closer to eleven-thirty if I get stuck doom-scrolling on my phone, which I know I shouldn't do, especially since one of my new rules was 'no screens an hour before bed.' I totally failed at that one. But anyway, once I actually put the phone down and turn off the lamp, I'm out like a light. I sleep all the way through the night, usually until my alarm goes off at seven. I don't wake up in the middle of the night in a panic or anything. 

And it's not like I'm sleeping *too* much, either. I'm not taking naps during the day, even when I feel that heavy, gross feeling I mentioned earlier. I just sit at my desk and feel bad instead of sleeping to escape it. So, yeah, my actual sleep schedule and the quality of my sleep haven't changed at all. It's almost like my brain is so exhausted from beating me up all day about not being organized enough that by the time night rolls around, it just completely shuts down. Which I guess is a good thing, because if I were exhausted from not sleeping on top of everything else, I don't even know how I'd function right now. But yeah, sleep is... sleep is completely normal.

Worthless? Um, I don't know if I'd use that exact word. Like, I don't sit around thinking I have zero value as a human being or that the world would be better off without me or anything extreme like that. But a failure? Yeah. Yeah, I definitely feel like a failure right now.

And then, because I'm dropping the ball on the creative stuff I actually like, I just feel this immense guilt about it all the time. But then instead of, like, sitting down and just catching up on the drafts or the notes like a normal person, I just end up feeling terrible and canceling plans with people so I can stay home, even though I don't even use that time to catch up. Irritable? Um... no, not really. I mean, I guess it depends on what you mean by irritable, but if you mean like snapping at people or getting annoyed easily, then no, I don't think so. 

Honestly, I don't really have a lot of opportunities to be irritable with anyone right now anyway. I live by myself, and since I've been so stuck on trying to get this whole schedule thing to work, I haven't exactly been going out and socializing much. My friends text me, of course, and we have this group chat from when we were all doing our associate's degrees together. They're always talking about their new jobs or asking if I want to meet up for coffee or drinks, and I don't get mad at them for it. I don't read their messages and feel annoyed. If anything, I just feel guilty that I don't have anything good to report back, so I end up just kind of ghosting the chat for a few days until I can think of something neutral to say that doesn't sound like I'm totally failing at life. But it's never irritation directed at them.

And even with myself, it's not really irritation. Like, when I'm sitting there staring at that expensive planner I bought, the one I spent hours researching, and it's just completely blank... I'm not angry or irritable. It's more of that heavy, overwhelming feeling I was talking about before. It's frustration, yeah, but it's a very inward, quiet kind of frustration. It's not like I want to throw the planner across the room or yell or anything. I just sit there and feel disappointed. 

I did read somewhere that sometimes anxiety or stress can make people really on edge and snappy, like their fuse is just super short, but I haven't noticed that happening with me. When I go to the grocery store or something—which is pretty much my only outing these days—I'm perfectly polite to the cashiers. I don't get annoyed if the person in front of me is taking too long or if they're out of the brand of oatmeal I wanted to buy for my perfectly planned healthy breakfasts that I'm not actually making. It's just... whatever. It doesn't bother me. All my emotional energy is just so tied up in this internal struggle of trying to figure out why I can't just do the things I set out to do, so there's not really any left over to be irritable about anything else. So, yeah, I wouldn't say I've been feeling irritable at all.

Trouble concentrating? Um, I don't think so. I mean, I guess it depends on what you're trying to concentrate on, right? Like, if you mean am I losing my train of thought all the time, or forgetting what I'm doing in the middle of doing it, then no, definitely not.

And when I actually *do* try to do something, like, say I decide I'm going to spend thirty minutes looking at job postings. I can read the postings just fine. I can understand all the requirements and the job descriptions. I don't lose focus while I'm reading them. It's just that the whole time I'm reading, my brain is screaming at me that I'm not qualified, or that I'm never going to get hired, or that I'm already so far behind everyone else from my associate's program. So I guess the concentration is there, but the motivation or the... the ability to actually *act* on what I'm concentrating on is what's missing. 

I was watching this documentary the other day—well, not a documentary, it was like a long YouTube video essay about productivity culture—and I watched the whole hour-long thing without getting distracted once. I absorbed all the information, I understood the arguments the creator was making, I didn't even pause it to go to the bathroom. So clearly my brain is capable of focusing on things. It just seems to refuse to focus on the things that would actually help me get my life together. So, yeah, I wouldn't say I have trouble concentrating. I just have trouble doing anything productive with that concentration.

Now, if I take a walk, I'm just thinking about how I'm wasting time, or how I should be doing something productive, or how I'm failing at being organized. So the walk isn't pleasurable anymore, it's just another thing I'm doing wrong. \n\nI don't know if that makes sense. It's just really frustrating because I want to enjoy things, I really do. I keep trying to force myself to do things that I know I usually like, hoping that the feeling will just magically come back. Like, 'okay, if I watch this funny movie, I'll laugh and feel better.' But then I watch it, and I might chuckle, but it doesn't reach that deeper level of actually feeling good. It's just all so surface-level right now, and underneath that surface, it's just this constant buzz of stress and guilt about not being the person I'm trying to be. Unable to experience pleasure? Um... no, I don't think so. I still like the things I've always liked. Um, how long? I guess... it's been about two months now. Yeah, two months. It all started right around the time I decided I was going to completely overhaul my entire routine and, like, my whole presentation as a person.
